n.quote:
Participants. Thirty-eight Buropean American students (17 men
and 21 women) from Stanford University and 38 Korean students (14 men
and 24 women) from Soongsil University in Seoul, South Korea, filled out
the questionnaire, Both groups were recruited from psychology classes.

notes:
Assigned original Study 2 is located and document identity matches Kim and Markus (1999), title and DOI. The generic description and locator p. 5 (printed p. 789) do not distinguish the culture main effect, Culture X Subfigure Ratio interaction, unique-subfigure comparison, plural-minority comparison, or culture-specific comparisons against midpoint. No target selected by row position or numeric matching. Candidate evidence only: Overall, European Americans liked
minority subfigures more than Koreans did, F(1, 69) = 22.28, p<
.01. Again, there was a Culture X Subfigure Ratio interaction, F(1,
69) = 4.32, p < .05.
Planned comparisons showed that liking for the unique subfigures
differed between European Americans (M = 5.88, SD = 2.11) and
Koreans (M = 3.81, SD = 1.91), (74) = 4.55, p < OL. Liking for
the plural minority subfigures also differed, although to a lesser
degree, between European Americans and Koreans (Ms = 5.63
and 4,33, SDs = 1.51 and 1.46, respectively), (69) = 3.68, p <
A! (see Figure 3).
Finally, when the means of liking were compared with the
midpoint (5), the analyses showed that European Americans’ lik-
ing for the unique subfigures was greater than the midpoint,
#35) = 2.50, p < .02, whereas Koreans’ liking for the unique
subfigures was less than the midpoint, (37) = 3.84, p < .01.
Study 2 reports F statistics, comparison statistics (with OCR-damaged test labels and some p bounds), means and SDs; no printed Cohen d is supplied for these tests. No metric conversion performed. The canonical p < OL and p < A! tokens are retained literally and are not silently repaired. Questionnaire contributor counts: 38 European American students and 38 Korean students. These are not an explicit final sample for a uniquely identified critical test; no analytic N sum or df-based inference made. No PDF path supplied, so layout/OCR verification unavailable within assigned source scope. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
